curated.instructions: omr/instructions/8859-1/ (scans; the tractor is pages 1-15, steps 1-20, the cultivator it pulls steps 21-25 on pages 14-16; the harrow on pages 16-17 and the other models after)

functions.does: The steering wheel steers the front wheels: its column runs forward through two universal joints to a 24-tooth gear over the front axle, which slides a toothed rack that pushes both steering arms.
functions.source: book: steps 3, 6-7 (steering arms and rack), 13-14 and 16 (column and wheel)
functions.note: Doesn't work today. The steering wheel's mounting (p460 3738, p463 3004, p464 3004, p465 3709b) and its axle are loose parts, so the wheel only turns that loose mounting. The column's 24-tooth gear p250 3648a turns the universal joints but doesn't mesh the rack p95 3743, and the rack hangs on hinges rather than sliding, so the steering arms flop.

functions.does: Rolling the tractor runs the engine: the rear wheels turn the differential, a 14-tooth bevel on the drive shaft takes the drive forward, and under the bonnet a 24-tooth gear, two 8-tooth idlers and a second 24-tooth gear turn a crankshaft built from gears, which pumps two pistons up and down.
functions.source: book: steps 1-3 (differential and drive shaft), 10 and 14-15 (engine gears and crankshaft); that rolling drives it is inferred from the gearing
functions.note: Partly works today: turning the drive shaft's front gear p411 3648a turns the crankshaft and works both pistons, but rolling doesn't reach it, as the drive shaft's bevel p7 4143 doesn't mesh the differential p0 73071.

functions.does: The differential lets the two rear wheels turn at different speeds in a corner.
functions.note: Today the rear wheels and the differential turn together as the tractor rolls; turning one rear wheel against the other isn't tried here. The second bevel p21 4143 on its short axle behind the differential (step 2) seems only to steady it (inferred).

functions.does: The lever by the seat raises and lowers the three-point hitch and the cultivator on it: it turns a cross shaft whose 24-tooth gear drives an 8-tooth gear on a shaft below, whose two 8-tooth gears slide two toothed beams, which rock the hitch's drop links and lift the two lower links.
functions.source: book: step 11 (the toothed beams), step 14 (the gears), step 18 inset (the 24-tooth gear and the lever on the cab's side), steps 21-25 (the cultivator); the lifting is inferred from the gearing, as the book draws no arrows
functions.note: Partly works today. The lever's handle p503 3706 hinges freely on its toggle joint p507 4273a, so it turns nothing; turning the 24-tooth gear p488 3648a slides the toothed beams and rocks the drop links p273 4273a and p274 4273a, but they aren't joined to the lower links, so the cultivator doesn't rise. The seat back (p398 3031 and its toggle joints, on the same cross shaft) tilts with the lever, which it shouldn't. The cultivator swings freely on the lower links' axle: its top link p116 3702 isn't joined to it.

functions.does: The front wheels turn freely on short axles in the steering arms.
The cultivator's four tines are held down by rubber bands and spring back when they hit something.
functions.skip: the rubber bands only matter under force; they aren't in the model file

functions.does: The cab frame, its sloping front legs, the bonnet and the exhaust stack stay rigid on the chassis.
functions.source: inferred: steps 17-20 pin the cab and bonnet to the chassis; nothing in the book swings
functions.note: Today the cab p482 3703 turns alone on its rear axle p57 3708, each front leg (p335, p336 3895) turns on its own on the axle p54 3737, and the bonnet p564 3666 swings on the right front leg.

questions.question: Does the lever raise the hitch? Does the bonnet hinge up?
